critical_issues.msg: CustomerStatus imported from models.customer has 4 values but VALID_STATUSES on line 18 has 7 values — 'partner', 'prospect', 'active', 'blocked' are in VALID_STATUSES but not in the enum; count_by_status() will crash with ValueError when it encounters these statuses.
critical_issues.suggestion: Extend CustomerStatus enum in models/customer.py to include all VALID_STATUSES values, or remove the missing ones from VALID_STATUSES. Ensure the two stay in sync.

critical_issues.msg: count_by_status() returns Dict[CustomerStatus, int] but the dict comprehension on line 146 calls CustomerStatus(row[0]) which raises ValueError for any status string not defined in the enum (e.g. 'partner', 'prospect', 'blocked').
critical_issues.suggestion: This line will raise at runtime for any status not in the enum. Either the enum must be exhaustive, or use a try/except (or .get()) to gracefully handle unknown statuses.

suggestions.msg: delete_customer returns dict {'id': customer_id} while all other service methods return ORM models — inconsistent return type for a mutation method.
suggestions.suggestion: Return type annotation is missing on line 129 (declared as -> dict) — consider returning just customer_id (int) or None to match other delete-style methods, or add an explicit type annotation.

suggestions.msg: _seed_user is defined in this file but only used by assign_owner (line 189) and a few SalesService tests — minor duplication vs the same helper in tests/integration/conftest.py.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider importing _seed_user from conftest.py or the shared helpers module to avoid duplication.

suggestions.msg: _seed_customer is defined in this file but may duplicate a helper of the same name in conftest.py — search for both definitions before adding another.
suggestions.suggestion: Consolidate into a single shared _seed_customer in conftest.py and import it here.

suggestions.msg: test_list_customers asserts 'len(items) >= 3' but creates only 3 customers for this specific tenant — if other tests share the same DB (schema truncated between tests, but session is function-scoped), the assertion may flakily pass on a larger-than-expected result set.
suggestions.suggestion: Use tenant-scoped filtering or a unique-enough suffix to guarantee the assertion measures only the test's own data.

suggestions.msg: test_list_customers_pagination asserts 'total1 >= 5' using a >= comparison that hides whether pagination actually works or whether earlier tests left residual data.
suggestions.suggestion: Assert 'total1 == 5' or otherwise isolate the test's data so the assertion is deterministic.

suggestions.msg: test_count_by_status_tenant_isolation creates customers for tenant2_id within a test on the same async_session without cleanup — if the session is function-scoped but shared across tests, cross-test contamination is possible.
suggestions.suggestion: Verify conftest.py truncates all tables (TRUNCATE CASCADE) between each test function to guarantee isolation, or add explicit cleanup.

suggestions.msg: mock_db_session fixture defines session.commit = MagicMock() (line 23) — commit should not appear on the mock since services must never call commit (rules 121/122); the mock should not include this method.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove session.commit = MagicMock() from the fixture. If a test needs to verify flush was called, assert flush directly rather than having commit on the mock.

suggestions.msg: fake_refresh is a regular (non-async) function but service.create_customer calls 'await self.session.refresh(customer)' — async code calling a sync coroutine will fail with 'coroutine was never awaited' at runtime.
suggestions.suggestion: Make fake_refresh an async def: 'async def fake_refresh(obj): ...' and call it as 'mock_db_session.refresh = fake_refresh' without await (the mock replaces the bound method).

suggestions.msg: Same issue as line 149 — fake_refresh is synchronous but session.refresh is awaited in create_customer.
Same issue as line 149 — fake_refresh is synchronous but service.create_customer awaits it.
Test class TestCreateCustomerService is not decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio — pytest-asyncio requires explicit marking for class-level async test classes.
suggestions.suggestion: Add @pytest.mark.asyncio above the class definition: '@pytest.mark.asyncio\nclass TestCreateCustomerService:'.
